housing.summary: Lyon's rental market is competitive, especially in central arrondissements (1er, 2e, 6e Presqu'ile and Part-Dieu). One-bedroom apartments in the centre typically rent in the low four-figure euro range. Landlords usually require a French guarantor or a Visale guarantee, proof of income (payslips ~3x rent), and often use an agency (frais d'agence). Furnished (meuble) and unfurnished lets have different lease terms.

banking.summary: Opening a French bank account requires proof of identity, proof of address (justificatif de domicile), and often a residence permit or long-stay visa. Major retail banks and online banks operate in Lyon. Newcomers frequently use online banks for faster onboarding while awaiting a proof of address.

schools.summary: Lyon has a strong public school system plus several international and bilingual options serving relocating families. International curricula are available through dedicated international schools; the Cite Scolaire Internationale de Lyon offers international sections within the public system. Enrolment in public schools is tied to the family's address (sectorisation).

legal_admin.summary: Non-EU arrivals must validate their long-stay visa (VLS-TS) with the OFII and, where required, hold a residence permit (titre de sejour) handled via the local prefecture (Prefecture du Rhone). EU nationals do not need a residence permit but should register locally for services. Many administrative steps are handled online.
legal_admin.registration_step: Validate the long-stay visa (VLS-TS) with OFII and obtain/renew a titre de sejour via the Prefecture du Rhone

tax_finance.summary: Residents are liable for French income tax and must obtain a tax identification number (numero fiscal / SPI) to file a return and access the online tax portal. Income tax is collected at source (prelevement a la source). New residents typically register with the tax administration after arrival.

transport.summary: Lyon has an extensive public transport network operated by TCL, covering metro, tram, funicular, and buses, complemented by the Velo'v bike-share scheme. Monthly passes are available at reduced rates for young people and students. Non-EU driving licences may need to be exchanged for a French licence depending on the country of issue and reciprocity agreements; healthcare access requires registering with the French social security system to obtain a carte Vitale.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: Non-EU/EEA licences may need exchange for a French permis de conduire subject to reciprocity; EU/EEA licences remain valid
transport.healthcare_registration: Register with Assurance Maladie (CPAM) to obtain a carte Vitale; affiliation via employer or under residence-based coverage
